## Decisions and why
- **A project is a folder with its own `.baton/HANDOFF.md`, found by scanning** —
  the rule `is_enabled` already applies, one level down. A declared list goes
  stale the moment someone renames a folder.
- **Depth 2 by default, `discovery.depth` to go deeper** — the scan runs on every
  session start of every project on the machine. Depth 3 is tens of thousands of
  stat calls and, under the cap, truncates arbitrarily.
- **The index grants nothing.** A list of what exists is not context and is not
  authorisation to work: the memory-mode decision, one level up.
- **The target is never inferred from the conversation — not even with a single
  project on disk.** 0.4.1 added that shortcut for convenience and 0.4.2 removed
  it: the count does not change what is being decided, which is whose handoff
  gets replaced.
- **Activation dies with the session**: cleared on `startup`/`clear`, kept on
  `compact`/`resume`/`fork`. Clearing it on compaction would drop the target
  exactly when the automatic cycle is about to ask for the handoff.
- **`Stop` stays silent with no resolvable target** — a question the hook cannot
  answer on its own is worse than saying nothing.

## Traps
- **Writing the draft moves the root.** `.baton/` is in `ROOT_MARKERS`, so
  creating `.baton/local/draft.md` turns that folder into a root, and the root
  moves between the `context` call and the `write` call. It caused two separate
  bugs (0.4.1, 0.4.2), and it silently invalidates any test that pre-creates a
  draft to set up a state: the test then measures its own setup.
- **`marketplace.json` carries its own `version`, apart from `plugin.json`.**
  Bumping only the second ships a release `claude plugin update` will not pick
  up, with no error anywhere. Guarded now by `tests/test_manifest.py`.
- **The README test-count guard fires on every commit that adds tests.** Update
  the badge and the prose line in both READMEs in the same commit or the suite is
  red.
- **Six bugs reached a real install with the whole unit suite green**, all found
  by running the scripts against a folder shaped like SECOP. The manual
  acceptance checks in the README are the only thing that sees them.
- **`tools/validate-mermaid.mjs` needs `npm install`**: install outside the repo
  and copy the script next to `node_modules`. `NODE_PATH` does not work for ESM.
